title.en: Z scheme and splitting of water

body.en: In PS II, the reaction centre absorbs 680 nm light; electrons are excited and passed to an electron acceptor, then down an electron transport chain of cytochromes to PS I. There the electrons are excited again by 700 nm light and passed to another acceptor and finally to NADP⁺, reducing it to NADPH + H⁺. This whole path, PS II → PS I → NADP⁺, is the *Z scheme* because of its shape when drawn on a redox scale. PS II replaces its lost electrons by splitting water: 2H₂O → 4H⁺ + O₂ + 4e⁻. The water-splitting complex is associated with PS II, which lies on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane, so the protons and oxygen are released into the lumen.

points.en: *Electrons* flow: H₂O → PS II → cytochromes → PS I → NADP⁺.
Water *splitting* is linked to PS II.
O₂ is a by-product of the light reaction.

title.en: The Z scheme and the proton gradient

narration.en: Let us draw the path of electrons from water to NADP⁺ and then see how ATP is made.

say.en: Light excites P680 in photosystem II. The electrons it loses are replaced by splitting water, which releases protons and oxygen.
The excited electrons run downhill through plastoquinone and the cytochrome complex, which pumps protons into the lumen.
Light excites P700 in photosystem I, and the electrons finally reduce NADP⁺ to NADPH. The zigzag looks like a Z.
Protons pile up inside the thylakoid lumen. They flow back to the stroma through ATP synthase, and that flow makes ATP.
Non-cyclic flow uses both photosystems and gives ATP, NADPH and oxygen. Cyclic flow uses only PS I in the stroma lamellae and gives only ATP.
Let us draw the path of electrons from water to NADP⁺ and then see how ATP is made.

caption.en: Light drives electrons through the transport chain. Protons build up inside the thylakoid lumen: from splitting water, from the carrier that pumps them across, and because NADP reductase removes H+ in the stroma. Protons flow back through the CF0 channel of ATP synthase, and CF1 makes ATP. In cyclic flow only PS I works: ATP is made but no NADPH or O2.

say.en: Shine light on a thylakoid and watch the protons pile up inside and stream out through ATP synthase.

body.en: ATP synthesis from ADP and inorganic phosphate in the presence of light is *photophosphorylation*. When both photosystems work in series, the electron flow is non-cyclic and produces ATP, NADPH and O₂. When only PS I works, the electron cycles back within the photosystem: cyclic flow, producing only ATP. Cyclic flow occurs in the stroma lamellae, whose membranes lack PS II and the NADP reductase enzyme, and when only light beyond 680 nm is available. ATP synthesis is explained by chemiosmosis: protons accumulate in the lumen (from water splitting and from the proton pumping by the electron carrier), and protons are removed from the stroma when NADP⁺ is reduced. The resulting proton gradient across the thylakoid membrane drives protons back to the stroma through the CF₀ channel of ATP synthase; the CF₁ head, protruding into the stroma, makes ATP.

points.en: Non-cyclic: PS II + PS I; ATP + NADPH + O₂.
Cyclic: PS I only; ATP only; stroma lamellae.
ATP synthase: CF₀ (channel in the membrane) + CF₁ (in the stroma).

say.en: Let us work through this together. How many molecules of water must be split to release 6 molecules of O 2, and how many electrons does this supply to PS II?
2H 2O gives 4H⁺ plus O 2 plus 4e⁻: two water molecules give one O 2 and four electrons.
For 6 O 2: 6 times 2 equals 12 H 2O.
Electrons released equals 6 times 4 equals 24 e⁻.
So the answer is 12 H 2O split; 24 electrons supplied.

homework.en: Draw the Z scheme and label PS II, PS I, the electron transport chain and NADP⁺.

narration.en: Recap. Z scheme: H₂O → PS II → PS I → NADP⁺. 2H₂O → 4H⁺ + O₂ + 4e⁻ at PS II. Non-cyclic gives ATP, NADPH, O₂; cyclic gives only ATP. Proton gradient across the thylakoid drives ATP synthase (CF₀–CF₁).
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. Z ಯೋಜನೆ: H₂O → PS II → PS I → NADP⁺. PS II ನಲ್ಲಿ ನೀರಿನ ವಿಭಜನೆ. ಚಕ್ರೀಯವಲ್ಲದ ಹರಿವು ATP, NADPH, O₂; ಚಕ್ರೀಯ ಹರಿವು ಕೇವಲ ATP. ಪ್ರೋಟಾನ್ ಇಳಿಜಾರು ATP ಸಿಂಥೇಸ್ ಅನ್ನು ಚಾಲನೆ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: Let us recall the key ideas. Z scheme: H 2O gives PS II gives PS I gives NADP⁺.
say.kn: ಮುಖ್ಯ ಅಂಶಗಳನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳೋಣ. Z ಯೋಜನೆ: H 2O gives PS II gives PS I gives NADP⁺.

say.en: 2H 2O gives 4H⁺ plus O 2 plus 4e⁻ at PS II.
Non-cyclic gives ATP, NADPH, O 2; cyclic gives only ATP.
say.kn: ಚಕ್ರೀಯವಲ್ಲದ ಹರಿವು ATP, NADPH, O 2; ಚಕ್ರೀಯ ಹರಿವು ಕೇವಲ ATP.
